newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm Council unlikely to agree on cereal penalty changes.
newsitem.headline: Farm Council unlikely to agree on cereal penalty changes.

text.p: European Union farm ministers are unlikely to agree next week on a proposal to make penalties for overplanting cereals and oilseeds more flexible, EU diplomats said.
Following a Spanish request, the European Commission has proposed exempting farmers who due to drought or other climatic disasters switched crops and exceeded national area limits.
In response to German demands, it has also proposed allowing governments to target penalties on farmers in regions which overplanted.
"Member states made extra demands. It has become incredibly complex," a diplomat said, adding the difficulties were mainly over the targetting of penalties.
Germany, France, Italy, Ireland, Spain and Portugal wanted greater flexibility and weaker penalties.
A compromise presented by the Irish EU presidency this week was rejected by the European Commission.
It said that the demands of member states would make the penalty system even more complex, raise production, cost more money and break GATT rules.
